scope: SQLite official testing.html snapshot; test sizes and coverage vary with SQLite version

claims.claim: SQLite is tested by four independent harnesses; the TCL tests are in the public domain and are the primary tests during development (harness ~27.2 KSLOC of C; 1390 script files, 23.2MB; 51445 distinct test cases, parameterized into millions)
claims.notes: Replaces the earlier chapter's invented '10x code size' and test-type percentage table

claims.claim: TH3 is a proprietary C test harness providing 100% branch and 100% MC/DC coverage; it uses only published interfaces and targets embedded platforms (~1055.4 KSLOC, 50362 cases; full-coverage run about 2.4M instances; prerelease soak about 248.5M tests)
claims.notes: TH3 is not in the public source tree; the earlier chapter's 'test/th3/ public' claim is wrong

claims.claim: The SQL Logic Test harness runs the same SQL against SQLite and PostgreSQL, MySQL, Microsoft SQL Server and Oracle 10g and compares answers (7.2 million queries, 1.12GB of test data)
dbsqlfuzz is a proprietary libFuzzer-based fuzzer that mutates both the SQL input and the database file; it has 336 seed files and runs about one billion mutations per day

SQLite claims 100% branch test coverage in an as-deployed configuration and, via TH3, 100% MC/DC; because C && and || short-circuit, branch coverage and MC/DC are very nearly the same, differing mainly in boolean-vector tests handled with testcase() macros
claims.locator: 1.1 Executive Summary and 7.4 Branch coverage versus MC/DC

claims.claim: Google OSS-Fuzz has tested SQLite since 2016; test/ossfuzz.c is SQLite's interface to it; it no longer finds historical bugs but occasionally finds issues in new development check-ins
claims.notes: The earlier chapter's dated list of specific fuzz bugs was removed as unsourced

claims.claim: The official position is that maintaining 100% MC/DC is laborious and probably not cost-effective for a typical application, but is justified for a widely-deployed infrastructure library and an anomaly-testing suite is required before each release
Anomaly testing covers out-of-memory, I/O error, crash/power-loss and compound failures; specialized programs include speedtest1.c, mptester.c, threadtest3.c, fuzzershell.c and jfuzz
